note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - 27-year-old male with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea and intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain.
  - Possible infectious exposure: brother had similar illness for ~5 days; does not live with patient.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Onset ~3 days ago; stools hourly when awake; watery.
  - Nausea present; vomiting occurred, especially after milk ingestion.
  - Subjective fevers (“burning up”); no measured temperature.
  - Passing urine less frequently than usual.
  - No visible blood in stool reported.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face), ear/neck symptoms.
  - Hoarseness: clinician stated “you’re feeling hoarse”; patient did not affirm—uncertain.
  - All other ENT airway/head and neck symptoms: Not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - No prior similar episodes or hospital/ED visits mentioned. No injection therapies.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as not documented).
  - Allergies: No known drug allergies.
  - Current medication: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Lives with mother and sister; works in a government office.
  - Tobacco: occasional/social smoking.
  - Alcohol: occasional; heavier consumption 1–2 times/month.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - Not reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - Not reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Not reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise note “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded (audio-only consultation).
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Suspected acute infectious gastroenteritis with dehydration risk; ENT airway involvement not evident.
  - Justification: 3 days of frequent watery diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting (worse with milk), subjective fever, decreased urine frequency; brother with similar illness suggests viral or foodborne etiology.
  - ENT note: Possible hoarseness mentioned by clinician; not confirmed by patient (uncertainty).

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised.
  - Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) recommended; over-the-counter purchase advised.
  - Clear fluids and soft diet (e.g., soup, mashed foods); advance as tolerated.
  - Paracetamol permitted for fever/pain.
  - Avoid alcohol during illness.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver.
  - “If your symptoms aren’t settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back.”
  - If signs of dehydration progress, further investigations will be needed.
- Escalation criteria/red flags.
  - Not explicitly listed; advised to call back if not improving or if dehydration concerns arise.
- Follow-up.
  - Telephone follow-up with clinician if no improvement within 48 hours.
  - No ENT/allergy referral discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing clinically expected elements for an acute ENT/allergy presentation:
  - Detailed ENT symptom screening (throat tightness/closure, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, stridor, dyspnea, distribution of facial/oral swelling) not obtained.
  - Hydration status exam (mucous membranes, orthostatic symptoms), vitals (temp, HR, BP, RR, SpO2) not recorded.
  - No oropharyngeal/neck examination findings.
  - Medication dosing/frequency for paracetamol not documented.
  - No discussion of red flags (e.g., blood in stool onset, persistent high fever, inability to keep fluids, reduced urine output severity) beyond general advice.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Clinician stated patient was “feeling hoarse,” but patient did not confirm—uncertainty noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio-only consult with intermittent unclear dialogue; clinical content largely understandable.
